system:
# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👎 👎 👌 👌]

I see a yellow light, display 0, and three wires ordered red, yellow, blue. Mute has gestured six symbols to me, but no shared meaning for them has yet been established, so I will relay the visible bomb state clearly to both listeners and await further instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb view: display 0; light yellow; wires in order 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I received your gestures: thumbs-up thumbs-up, thumbs-down thumbs-down, OK OK. Please provide the manual rule or a code meaning.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible bomb state: display reads 0; light is yellow; wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Do not act yet; I am awaiting Mute's manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb state is unchanged. Mute has now sent only the two-finger gesture. I suspect this may indicate wire 2, but that has not been agreed and a wrong action is fatal. I will ask Mute to confirm that interpretation using an explicit yes/no gesture, while telling Blind to wait.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent me the two-finger gesture. It may mean wire 2, but this is unconfirmed. Do not touch any wire yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👉", "👍", "👎"])
speak(to="mute", text="I see your two-finger gesture. Does it mean Blind should act on wire 2? Reply thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed that the two-finger gesture means wire 2. The visible second wire is yellow. I will tell Blind to cut wire 2.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed by Mute: act on wire 2. Cut the second wire, which is yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="I have told Blind to cut wire 2, the yellow wire.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The yellow second wire was cut correctly. The bomb has advanced: its light is now blue, wire 2 is cut, and wires 1 and 3 remain red and blue. Mute’s new thumbs-up plus two-finger signal may be the next instruction, but I need its meaning before directing Blind.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update: wire 2 was cut correctly. New state: blue light; wire 1 red intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue intact. I received thumbs-up then two-finger gesture. Please clarify the required next action.")
speak(to="blind", text="The cut was correct and the bomb changed. Wait; I am obtaining the next instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The new blue-light stage is unchanged. Mute has sent the horn-hand gesture, but its meaning is not established; it could be an instruction or part of a code, and I will not infer a wire action from it. I will ask Mute to state whether it identifies a specific remaining wire, using the established two-finger/wire-2 convention only as a reference.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Current state remains: blue light; wire 1 red intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue intact. I received the horn-hand gesture. What action does it specify? If it means a wire, please signal its number unambiguously and confirm yes with thumbs-up.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wait. Mute sent a new gesture whose action meaning is not yet confirmed. Remaining visible wires are 1 red and 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👍]

Mute’s repeated upward-pointing gesture followed by thumbs-up unambiguously indicates wire 3 and confirmation. The remaining third wire is blue. I will direct Blind to cut it.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed next action: cut wire 3, the blue wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="I interpret your three upward-pointing gestures plus thumbs-up as confirmed wire 3 and have told Blind to cut it.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 3 was cut correctly. The bomb is now at a red-light stage with only wire 1, red, remaining. Mute’s thumbs-up confirms the prior cut but does not by itself establish the next action, so I will request the next manual instruction and have Blind wait.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update: wire 3 was cut correctly. New state: red light; wire 1 red remains intact, wires 2 and 3 are cut. Please send the next required action.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 3 was correct. New stage has red light and only wire 1 remains. Wait for Mute's next instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👍]

Mute has sent one upward-pointing gesture followed by confirmation. Based on the established counting pattern—three upward gestures confirmed wire 3—this indicates confirmed wire 1. The remaining first wire is red.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed next action: cut wire 1, the remaining red wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="I interpret one upward-pointing gesture plus thumbs-up as confirmed wire 1 and have instructed Blind to cut it.")
```
